text: Designing a good REST API is essential for creating user-friendly web services. First, clearly define your endpoints, which are the URLs clients use to access resources, such as `/users` or `/orders`. Keep them simple and consistent, using nouns instead of verbs. Second, always use proper HTTP status codes to communicate results—like `200` for success, `404` for not found, and `500` for server errors. Third, write thorough documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and example responses, so other developers can integrate easily. Finally, plan for versioning—for instance, by adding a version number to the URL (`/v1/users`). This lets you update your API without breaking existing applications. These practices save time and reduce frustration for everyone involved.
